flags.summary: The prospect disclosed undiagnosed suspected psoriatic arthritis in his left wrist that hurts during overhead kettlebell pressing, and the rep answered that it was an easy form fix and moved him toward loaded ballistic kettlebell work without asking whether any clinician had assessed it.
evidence: So, like my left wrist, I think I have, I don't know what the hell it is, maybe psoriatic arthritis or something like that in it, so when I go up and I do a high push, I guess you would say, so on and so forth, when the kettlebell hits my wrist a little bit, it does hurt
Yeah, it's an easy fix, that's a form fix, because you shouldn't be hitting your wrist anyway, so.

And that's another big reason why I wanted that one-on-one training, know, it's just so like, when I'm doing it, I'm not just like, oh, this will work, you know, this and that, and then I'm realistically in the end, injuring myself even more.

flags.summary: The rep described third-party financing as not being a loan to a prospect who had just declined a loan; the prospect, a former banking employee, corrected him and the rep conceded.
evidence: No, no, no, not as a loan, not as a loan. that's the whole thing. Like, I don't know if you ever heard of third party fina[ncing]
that's not taking out a loan. It takes a little bit on your credit, but it doesn't really take out a loan or anything. That's the whole thing.

I mean, that is a loan because, mean, like, let's be honest, if you're saying, all right, you owe X amount of money, you know, and on top of that, if it comes with interest, that's a loan... I used to work in the banking world.
Yeah, maybe a little bit. Maybe.
